---
title: "Single-layer air-core solenoid: inductance"
subtitle: "Magnetics"
toc: true
---

A quick derivation of solenoid inductance from first principles, then the practical correction engineers actually use, with a calculator to try real turn counts and dimensions.

## The ideal case

Treating the coil as infinitely long, Ampere's law gives a uniform field inside: $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n = N / l$ is turns per unit length. Flux linkage through all $N$ turns gives:

$$
L_{ideal} = \mu_0 N^2 \frac{\pi r^2}{l}
$$

This overestimates inductance for any real, finite coil — it ignores fringing at the ends.

![Fig. 1 — field concentrated inside the winding, with fringing paths returning outside.](../assets/img/solenoid-field.png)

## Wheeler's correction

For a real single-layer coil where length isn't much greater than radius, Wheeler's 1928 approximation is the standard practical formula ($r$, $l$ in inches, result in $\mu H$):

$$
L_{\mu H} \approx \frac{r^2 N^2}{9r + 10l}
$$

Valid roughly for $l > 0.4r$. Below that, it undercorrects and a full Nagaoka-coefficient treatment is needed.

![Fig. 2 — field strength rising with current, fringing appearing at the ends.](../assets/img/coil-animation.gif)

## Calculator

```{=html}
<div id="solenoid-calc"></div>
<script src="../assets/js/calc-engine.js"></script>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "solenoid-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "N", label: "Turns N", value: 50, min: 1, step: 1 },
    { id: "r", label: "Radius r (cm)", value: 1.5, min: 0.1, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "l", label: "Length l (cm)", value: 4, min: 0.1, step: 0.1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "ideal", label: "Ideal L" },
    { id: "wheeler", label: "Wheeler L" },
    { id: "ratio", label: "Ideal / Wheeler" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    var MU0 = 4 * Math.PI * 1e-7;
    var rM = v.r / 100, lM = v.l / 100;
    var A = Math.PI * rM * rM;
    var lIdealUH = (lM > 0 ? (MU0 * v.N * v.N * A) / lM : 0) * 1e6;
    var rIn = v.r / 2.54, lIn = v.l / 2.54;
    var denom = 9 * rIn + 10 * lIn;
    var lWheelerUH = denom > 0 ? (rIn * rIn * v.N * v.N) / denom : 0;
    return {
      ideal: lIdealUH.toFixed(2) + " uH",
      wheeler: lWheelerUH.toFixed(2) + " uH",
      ratio: lWheelerUH > 0 ? (lIdealUH / lWheelerUH).toFixed(2) + "x" : "-"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
